messages:
Sam: Heads up — we need to settle the calibration dataset strategy for the next INT8/FP8 rollout. Quick poll: representative distribution vs adversarial/outlier-heavy? Also we should decide per-channel vs per-tensor. I'm seeing kernel-selection and KV-cache interactions in profiling that change performance significantly.
Laura: I'm in favor of a representative dataset + targeted heavy-tail sampling. Outliers should be handled explicitly (clipping or separate pass), not mixed into the main calib set. From profiling, occasional extreme activations push the kernel selector to a slower fallback.
Mike: +1 on treating outliers separately. But don't hide them — they happen in prod. My proposal: main rep calib for performance/kernels, then an "adversarial" suite to validate accuracy and fallback behavior.
Anya: Agreed with Mike. FWIW per-channel gave better quant MSE but the runtime overhead (indexing + non-contiguous loads) caused batching perf to drop ~6ms/token in our 4-bit traces. We should measure both perf and coverage.
Sam: Can you paste the profiling snippet from the last run where perf regressed?
Anya: Sure — here's a trimmed excerpt from the profiler run on staging.
```
profile: model=redwood-3B-quant
kernel=4bit_per_channel
batch_size=16
kv_cache=enabled
median_token_latency_ms=24.2
p95_token_latency_ms=48.9
int8_mse=0.0078
calibration=per-channel_sample_1k_main + 200_outlier_examples
notes=kernel_selector_fell_back_to_scalar_path_on_layer_8
```
Devon: Nice capture. I traced the fallback — it's because the per-channel layout we emitted breaks the expected packed stride for the fast vectorized kernel, so the runtime does an element-wise path and extra KV memcpy. Changing the packing to aligned 64-byte blocks fixed the copies and improved latency ~12% in local tests.
Laura: Important tradeoff: per-tensor is simpler and keeps memory contiguous -> better batching and KV cache locality, but it hurts tail accuracy on layers with high activation variance.
Mike: We need an automatic metric. Suggest 'calibration coverage' = percent of tokens with activations within calibration range. If coverage < 98% trigger adversarial calibration and enable stricter regression alerts. Also surface "fallback count" per model version.
Sam: I like the coverage metric. Action items: Laura — implement representative sampling pipeline (stratified by seq len & domain); Mike — build adversarial mini-suite and define coverage threshold; Devon — validate kernel packing/layout fix on our staging GPU fleet; Anya — rerun perf with alignment-aware batching. Target: canary next Tue. :thumbsup:
profiling-bot: Perf test `int8-rollout/staging` started for sha: a1b2c3d (scheduled by Sam).
Anya: One more operational note: the batching heuristic must be quant-kernel-aware — vector width/alignment matters. We saw misaligned sequence boundaries cause an extra copy before kernel call. Need a small hook in the runtime to prefer batch boundaries aligned to kernel lanes.
Devon: I'll add an alignment-aware batching hook (runtime) and a layout-conformance check during model compile.
Sam: Great. I'll summarize and write a short RFC. If anyone hits blockers with dataset access or QA infra ping me.
Laura: I'll start sampling script today and post the dataset manifest here.
Mike: I'll sketch the adversarial prompts (long-tail tokens, code, math, low-freq entities) and add them to CI.
Devon: I'll run a quick canary after the packing patch lands; will report exact delta and attach flamegraphs.
Anya: Thanks — keep an eye on p95 for KV-heavy workloads; that's where we see regressions.
Sam: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the first perf-run.
